applicability_values.conditional: Stage runs only when its condition holds (stated in the depth note).
applicability_values.skip: Stage does not run at this tier.

cross_cutting.name: Adversarial pass (Section 2)
cross_cutting.rule: Every AI-generated plan, canvas, architecture choice, or scope gets one explicit self-critique (weakest assumption, most likely failure, at least one alternative framing, conflicts with earlier evidence) and explicit user sign-off before it is locked into master-prd.md.

T3.depth: Opportunity Solution Tree; prioritize with Opportunity Score (default), ICE, or RICE for larger backlogs.

T4.depth: Opportunity Solution Tree; RICE for larger backlogs, ICE for fast triage, Kano for delight-vs-satisfy.

frameworks.name: Opportunity Solution Tree (outcome → opportunities → solutions → assumption tests)
Opportunity Score (Importance × (1 − Satisfaction))
frameworks.condition: More than one candidate solution or feature.

frameworks.name: ICE (Impact × Confidence × Ease)
frameworks.condition: More than one candidate solution or feature.

frameworks.name: Kano model
frameworks.condition: Default at T4; at any active tier when UX differentiation matters.

frameworks.name: MoSCoW (final scope-lock mechanism — executed in Stage 7)

T2.depth: No viability framework applies below T3.

frameworks.name: Precise market definition (geography, population, need, category — never "everyone")
TAM/SAM/SOM with sourced assumptions (mandatory at T4; optional lightweight at T3)
Competitor/alternative table incl. "do nothing" and manual-process alternatives

T3.depth: MoSCoW; RICE/ICE numeric tie-breaking if the backlog is large.

T4.depth: Full MoSCoW requirements pass; RICE/ICE numeric tie-breaking if the backlog is large.

frameworks.name: RICE/ICE numeric tie-breaking
frameworks.condition: Backlog large enough to need numeric tie-breaking.

T3.depth: Hook Model + AARRR + North Star Metric; HEART if the team already has product-analytics maturity.

T4.depth: Hook Model + AARRR + HEART + North Star Metric.

frameworks.name: Hook Model (Trigger → Action → Variable Reward → Investment)
HEART framework
frameworks.condition: Also at T3 if the team already has product-analytics maturity.

frameworks.name: North Star Metric (feeds the Opportunity Solution Tree's top node)

T1.depth: Only if there is a user-facing UI: a preset palette and font pairing (about six tokens), contrast-checked, and the one demo flow.

T2.depth: Only if there is a user-facing UI: full token set (colour roles, type scale, spacing, radius) with light/dark, contrast-checked; critical user flows and screen list.

T3.depth: Only if there is a user-facing UI: T2 set + motion, component inventory with states, voice and tone, empty/error/loading rules; design non-negotiables locked into master-prd.md.

T4.depth: Only if there is a user-facing UI: T3 set + client brand compliance, WCAG 2.2 AA audit plan, localisation plan when multi-market; design sign-off logged.

frameworks.name: Design tokens in a machine-readable backbone-tokens block (colour roles, fonts; type scale, spacing, radius at T2+; motion at T3+)
WCAG contrast check on every declared colour pair (4.5:1 text, 3:1 large text and UI)
Critical user flows (happy path + top failure paths) and screen inventory — one demo flow at T1
Localisation / i18n plan
frameworks.condition: More than one locale or market (see Stage 6).

frameworks.name: Client brand compliance
frameworks.condition: A client brand or style guide exists.

T1.depth: Informal feasibility lenses; mandatory real-vs-stubbed list.

T2.depth: Feasibility lenses; lightweight ADRs; C4 Context only; real-vs-stubbed. Security: threat model, secrets and auth decisions in security.md.

T3.depth: Feasibility lenses; Build/Buy/Partner; ADRs; C4; real-vs-stubbed; module boundary map + interface contracts. Security: threat model + data classification in security.md; domain glossary.

T4.depth: Formal feasibility lenses; Build/Buy/Partner; formal ADRs; C4; real-vs-stubbed; module boundary map + interface contracts. Security: threat model, data classification, PII inventory, retention and compliance mapping in security.md; domain glossary; run-cost per ADR.

frameworks.name: Feasibility lenses (technical, resource, timeline, risk) — formality scales by tier
ADRs (lightweight at T2, formal at T4)
C4 Model (Context-only at T2; Context/Container/Component/Code at T3+)
What must be real vs. what can be stubbed (mandatory at T1)
Module boundary map + interface contracts + dependency graph
Threat model (STRIDE-lite per trust boundary) + secrets handling + authn/authz decisions
Data classification + PII inventory + retention/deletion
frameworks.condition: Mandatory at T4; at T3 when the project stores personal data.

frameworks.name: Compliance regime mapping (GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2, PCI DSS, ...)
Domain glossary (one name per concept, used in code and interfaces)

T1.depth: master-prd.md + architecture.md + single work-packages.md; migrations if persistence; prerequisites + .env.example if external dependencies. Hand off to Spec Kit.

T2.depth: master-prd.md + architecture.md + single work-packages.md; migrations if persistence; prerequisites + .env.example if external dependencies. Hand off to Spec Kit.

T3.depth: master-prd.md + architecture.md (with claim/lock table) + per-module PRDs; migrations; prerequisites + .env.example. Hand off to BMAD or parallel subagents.

T4.depth: master-prd.md + architecture.md (with claim/lock table) + per-module PRDs; migrations; prerequisites + .env.example. Hand off to BMAD or parallel subagents.

frameworks.name: Verification gates (Given/When/Then + named gate per requirement)

T2.depth: Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then) + Definition of Done. Light test strategy.

T3.depth: Acceptance criteria + Definition of Done + qualitative checklist. Test strategy.

T4.depth: Acceptance criteria + Definition of Done + qualitative checklist. Test strategy.

frameworks.name: Qualitative checklist (clarity, evidence, feasibility, failure modes)
Test strategy (pyramid split, E2E critical paths from the user flows, test data, coverage target)

T1.depth: Where the demo runs, a one-command start, a recorded backup of the demo, and a pre-demo checklist.

T2.depth: Environments, CI that runs the verification gates, the deploy path, a rollback plan, and basic error logging.

T3.depth: T2 + rollout strategy (flags/canary/staged), observability tied to the North Star Metric, a runbook, and a risk-register review before launch.

T4.depth: T3 + SLOs and alerting, an incident process, change-approval/compliance evidence, and a backup/restore drill.

frameworks.name: Environments + CI/CD (the backbone-gates run in CI too)
Observability (errors at T2; logs, metrics and alerts tied to the North Star Metric at T3+)

T1.depth: Reverse-engineer from the judging rubric; Hook → Solution → Live demo → Tech+impact → Close; recorded backup.

T2.depth: Lighter positioning/differentiation pass; narrative for a demo or landing page.

T3.depth: Lighter positioning/differentiation pass; narrative for a demo or landing page.

T1.depth: Feedback loop applies after ship at T2+.

T2.depth: After ship: weekly real-user touchpoints, re-score Customer Validation Score, re-run the relevant discovery branch.

T3.depth: After ship: weekly real-user touchpoints toward the North Star Metric, re-score Customer Validation Score, re-run the relevant OST branch.

T4.depth: After ship: weekly real-user touchpoints toward the North Star Metric, re-score Customer Validation Score, re-run the relevant OST branch.

documents.purpose: Project-level tier + per-stage completion status.
One-page compressed opportunity statement.
5W2H, JTBD, HMW — raw problem-framing groundwork (Stage 2 prior-art findings recorded here too).
Mom Test notes, Opportunity Hypothesis block, full Customer Validation Score with reasoning per sub-score.
Living risk register: seeded by the pre-mortem, reviewed before release.
Filled Lean Canvas / Value Proposition Canvas.
Opportunity Solution Tree — living file with change history; also the feedback-loop mechanism.
Market type, buyer/user/payer map, sourced TAM/SAM/SOM, segmentation, competitor table, unit economics.
Hook Model, AARRR/HEART reasoning behind the North Star Metric.
Design tokens (backbone-tokens block), contrast checks, user flows, component and voice rules.
Chronological why-record, including adversarial passes and interface freezes.
Pitch/rubric mapping (T1) or positioning notes (T2–4).
Dated post-ship entries: what users said, updated score, resulting discovery-tree changes.
The non-negotiables.
ADRs, C4, real-vs-stubbed; module boundary map, interface contracts, dependency graph, claim/lock table at T3+.
Threat model, secrets, auth; data classification, PII and compliance at T3+/T4.
Single work-package file when only one agent is working.
Self-contained per-module PRD.
Test pyramid, E2E critical paths, test data, coverage target.
Demo plan (T1) or environments, CI/CD, rollout, rollback, observability, runbook (T2+).
Ordered, commented SQL migrations.
Credentials/prerequisites list.
Every environment variable, no real values (project root).
